newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan bourse in wait-and-see mood on peace moves.
newsitem.headline: Jordan bourse in wait-and-see mood on peace moves.

text.p: Jordanian stocks were steady Sunday as a wait-and-see mood gripped traders awaiting the outcome of MidEast peace talks, dealers said.
Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose a slight 0.07 percent to 147.73 points from 147.63 points on Saturday.
A total of 219,608 shares changed hands in 454,646 dinars volume. Of 43 stock traded, 16 advanced, eight declined and 19 were unchanged.
Brokers said investors stayed focused on peace talks that resumed Sunday between Israeli and Palestinian negotiators.

Market leader Arab Bank, which propelled the index up in the first half of September, lacked impetus. Its stock, the most expensive on the Amman exchange, was unchanged at 242.500 dinars in very low volume.

After gradual gains end of last month that sent the market back above 150 points last week for the first time in four months, shares began to weaken after clashes flared in the Israeli occupied West Bank last week.
The market was hit this year by the breakdown of Middle East peace talks and the delay in implementing a limited oil-for-food deal with Jordan's biggest trading partner Iraq.
Industrials led the market on Sunday with Jordan Petroleum Refinery dominating activity on healthy turnover of 111,665 dinars and a 0.10-dinar rise to 9.29 dinars.
Private Pearl Investable Index of 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.14 percent to 81.33 points, still 14.85 percent down from the same time last year.
